title: Make Hestia's sweep own and schedule Athena's recurring duties
summary: Add a duty table (docs/design/hestia.md and a matching code table in hestia.rs) listing the error-review pass, evidence-label derivation, code-health check, periodic design review and threshold checks with cadence (drain start, landing, every N landings) and where each runs. The sweep runs each due duty and records its last run; `athena status` shows last run and next due for each duty and flags overdue ones. Audience: the owner/operator reading status and design doc.

defaults_applied.how: Criteria run tests exercising cadence and overdue behavior.
Design doc table and changelog written for outside readers.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: read crates/athena-core/src/hestia.rs (Check trait, default_checks, run_sweep, ReadingRulesCheck), crates/athena-core/src/status.rs (StatusView, ReadingRuleStats, status()) and the record types in crates/athena-data/src/records.rs (AnyRecord, HestiaSweep). run_sweep runs all checks every time with no cadence; last-run state has to be persisted, most likely as a new field or record in athena-data; if a new record file is added it must pass check_record_file, AnyRecord and the round-trip test.

Last-run is stored as records (a duty-run record or a field on the sweep record) and 'every N landings' is counted from landed jobs in records; the exact mechanism is the producer's call after reading the code.

Duties are run through the existing Check trait or a thin Duty wrapper; existing implementations of the error review, throughput and reading-rule checks are reused, and duties with no implementation yet are registered with a clear 'not yet automated' outcome rather than invented.
No change to athena.toml, defaults.toml or workflows is needed; none is a deliverable.
Cadence N values are chosen by the producer and documented in the table.

acceptance_criteria.text: A test in crates/athena-core/src/hestia.rs, run by `cargo test -p athena-core`, builds a duty table with a drain-start, a per-landing and an every-N-landings duty. It shows one sweep runs each due duty and records its last run, and a second sweep within the cadence runs none.

A test in crates/athena-core/src/status.rs, run by `cargo test -p athena-core`, shows the status view flags a duty whose last run is past its cadence as overdue and does not flag a duty within its cadence. It also shows each duty with last run and next due point.

docs/design/hestia.md has one table listing every duty (error-review backlog pass, evidence-label derivation, code-health check, periodic design review, keep-rule threshold check, reading-rule refusal-rate check) with owner Hestia's sweep, cadence and where it runs. Grep of the file finds each duty name.
The duty table in hestia.rs lists the same duties and cadences as the table in docs/design/hestia.md, checked by a diff read or a test comparing ids.
`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test` all pass.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry describing the duty schedule, last-run records and status overdue flag.
Any new or changed record type under crates/athena-data is covered by `check_record_file`, `AnyRecord` and the round-trip test in records.rs, and old records still parse.

out_of_scope: Building new implementations of duties that do not exist yet beyond registering them
Changing the threshold values of the keep rule or reading-rule refusal flags
Changes to athena.toml, defaults.toml or CI workflows
departures: Larger than the reference: touches the sweep, status, a record type and the design doc, and needs persisted state.
hard_reason: Changes the Hestia sweep, which runs recurring checks and flags overdue work, and the status view that reports it, so a mistake would be hard to see.
